purpose: Visual routing preferences for future whole-house draft proposals. Raster images are not canonical engineering geometry.

sources.label_meaning: Likely complete circuit length in metres, but the raster has no visible unit legend.
observations: One whole-floor layout with approximately nine colour-separated circuit territories.
A dense collector/transit convergence area is visible near the lower centre.
Large regular rooms use counterflow spiral bodies.
Narrow and composite territories use elongated meanders or connected lobes.
Some circuits serve a main room plus a connected small or corridor-like area.
Two adjacent upper-right territories carry the same visible label 53, showing deliberate local balancing.

sources.label_meaning: Likely complete circuit length in metres, but the raster has no visible unit legend.
observations: Two separate whole-plan examples show regular, narrow and angled territories.
Long narrow territories use longitudinal meanders instead of forced rectangular spirals.
Chamfered and wedge-shaped territories use routes parallel to their boundaries.
Compact parallel transit bundles pass through concentrated openings and fan out with staggered bends.
Grey or blank regions are avoided, but their exact architectural meaning cannot be inferred from pixels alone.

circuit_identity: One stable colour represents one independent circuit.
Every circuit is treated as one continuous supply-to-return route.
Two separate route legs return to one compact collector area; circuits do not share a pipe trunk.
territory_planning: Partition by heatable territory, route feasibility and circuit length rather than enforcing one room per circuit.
Split a large space when one circuit would become too long or geometrically awkward.
Combine a small room, corridor or local lobe with an adjacent territory when a separate circuit would be impractical.
Do not create an artificial unheated strip at a mathematical partition.
Balance neighbouring circuits serving one large space when geometry permits, but do not add purposeless detours for exact equality.

topology_selection.high_aspect_room: elongated counterflow spiral or longitudinal meander
topology_selection.narrow_strip_or_corridor: regular parallel meander with compact U-returns
topology_selection.angled_or_wedge_room: boundary-conformal nested passes with a compact local hairpin
topology_selection.connected_irregular_zones: explicit composite route with one continuous neck between lobes

collector_and_transits: Plan the collector corridor and transit lane order before filling room bodies.
Use one compact collector area with two distinct pipes per circuit.
Keep transits as separate, parallel, noncrossing lanes through common corridors.
Preserve deterministic lane order through the narrowest bundle section.
Peel circuit pairs from the bundle close to their territory entry.
Use staggered bends to fan out without crossings or shared segments.
Pass walls only through explicit doors, openings or declared service gates.
Include transit length in complete circuit length.
room_body_and_turns: Follow the usable perimeter first, then continue inward while a meaningful offset remains.
Switch explicitly to a meander or local lobe when an irregular territory can no longer accept a regular frame.
Use compact clean spiral hairpins and regular meander U-returns.
Do not introduce staircase patterns or arbitrary short lateral segments into a spiral body.
Do not silently convert diagonal architectural boundaries into orthogonal stair steps.
Avoid walls and obstacles with an explicit clearance and bend envelope.

length_policy.visible_reference_range: approximately 42 to 70, likely metres but unconfirmed
objective_order: sensible territory and short transit assignment
local balance between circuits serving the same large room

next_blank_plan_workflow: Calibrate the raster from one explicit known dimension; never infer millimetres from pixels alone.
Trace and confirm floor boundary, room polygons, solid walls, doors/openings and obstacles.
Confirm exterior-wall identity and collector position/orientation.
Create heatable territories without artificial blank partitions.
Allocate separate collector transit lanes and wall gates before generating room bodies.
Select spiral, elongated spiral, meander or composite topology per territory morphology.
Generate every circuit as one ordered route, analyse it, and keep the result DRAFT until owner review.
